1  ORDER
This Criminal Original Petition has been filed seeking to quash the impugned FIR in Crime No. 26 of 2022 on the file of the first respondent police.

2.The learned Counsel for the petitioner would submit that the second respondent lodged a false complaint as against the petitioner alleging that the second respondent had a property in S.F.No.15/4D1B at Kondapethan Village, Madurai West Taluk, Madurai District.

While so, on 18.04.2022, the defacto complainant came to know that the petitioner and other accused have created a fake Aadhar Card and sale deed in the name of the defacto complainant and impersonated the defacto complainant and fraudulently sold the said property to one G.Jeevasugusathiyanathan.

Therefore, based on the complaint lodged by the defacto complainant, they registered a case in Crime No.26 of 2022, https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/05/2025 04:55:23 pm )
for the offence under Sections 120B, 419, 420, 465, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
In fact, the petitioner is not a named accused in the FIR, however, in the alteration report, his name has been included with an ulterior motive.
There are only vague and bald allegations against the petitioner and no any offence made out against the petitioner.

The cheque amount of Rs.5 Lakhs was paid to the petitioner through cheque from the account of the wife of the defacto complainant, namely, Vincenta Tamilarasi and apart from that no allegation against the petitioner and only based on the confession statement, the petitioner has been included as accused.
He would further submit that the above said sale deed has been subsequently cancelled.
Therefore, the impugned FIR is liable to be quashed.

3.The learned Government Advocate (Crl.Side) appearing for the respondent police would submit that based on the complaint lodged by the second respondent, they registered the present FIR in Crime No.26 of 2022, for the offence under Sections 120B, 419, 420, 465, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC.
Thereafter, investigation has been conducted and during investigation, they came to know that this petitioner also involved in this case.
Therefore, he has been included in this case.

The petitioner also https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 13/05/2025 04:55:23 pm ) received a sum of Rs.5 Lakhs through cheque from the account of the wife of the defacto complainant and thereby, his name also included in this case as one of the accused.
Now the case is under investigation.
Therefore, this petition is liable to be dismissed.

4.The learned Counsel for the second respondent would submit that the petitioner along with others have involved in impersonation and cheating and creation of forged documents and thereby, the second respondent lodged the complaint before the first respondent and registered the present FIR in Crime No.26 of 2022, for the offence under Sections 120B, 419, 420, 465, 467, 468 and 471 of IPC and now the same is under investigation.
During the investigation, it is found that the petitioner also involved in the occurrence.
Therefore, the matter needs elaborate investigation.

Hence, at this stage,
this petition is liable to be dismissed.
5.Heard both sides and perused the materials available on record.

sentences.text: 6.It is an admitted fact that the petitioner is not a named accused and the defacto complainant has not mentioned the petitioner's name in https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis

( Uploaded on:
13/05/2025 04:55:23 pm ) the complaint and thereafter, based on the confession statement of the co-accused, the petitioner was impleaded as one of the accused persons.

Even as per the prosecution, the petitioner only received a sum of Rs.5 Lakhs from one Raja through cheque from the account of the wife of the defacto complainant and there are no any other materials as against the petitioner and only on the allegations of receiving a sum of Rs.5 Lakhs from the main accused Raja from the account of the wife of the defacto complainant, he has been arrayed as accused in this case, that too based on the confession statement of the co-accused, he has been implicated.
Therefore, even as per the FIR there are no materials to constitute the offence as against the petitioner and without any materials, the petitioner has been included as accused in this case.
Even as per the FIR, the main accused Raja insisted the defacto complainant to issue cheque in favour of the petitioner/Ramesh for the purchase of property through agreement.
The petitioner no way related to the transaction between the defacto complainant and the main accused.
Moreover, the cheque was issued to the petitioner on the instruction of other accused, therefore, the petitioner cannot be roped into in this case.
Therefore, the impugned FIR is liable to be quashed.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
7.Accordingly, the impugned FIR in Crime No.26 of 2022 is quashed as against the petitioner.
In the result, this Criminal Original Petition is allowed.
Consequently, the connected miscellaneous petition is closed.
